f1c3d48d8664.text: Gain must be chosen with headroom and noise

1044b931dd62.text: The photodiode current is converted to voltage through the LMP7721 feedback network. The current BOM specifies a 100 MΩ feedback resistor and 2.2 pF compensation capacitor. For a 2.5 V, 16-bit converter, the ideal code interval is 2.5 / 2¹⁶ = 38.15 µV; dividing by 100 MΩ gives 0.381 pA per code. That is a quantization calculation, not an experimental detection limit. Leakage, dark current, drift, noise and optical background must be measured before choosing a useful gain range.

47006556dc63.text: The 100 MΩ / 2.2 pF parallel feedback network has a simple RC pole near 723 Hz. This is an estimate of that network, not a complete amplifier-stability calculation. Photodiode and input capacitance, board parasitics and amplifier response also contribute; settling, noise and frequency response remain bench tests.

406a8290c882.text: AeroSense is a compact reader designed to compare odor-responsive living-cell samples through fluorescence. It combines four replaceable 100 µL wells under a shared gas chamber, four frequency-tagged blue LEDs, one filtered photodiode, an ESP32-based acquisition circuit and a local phone interface. An eight-part printed enclosure fixes the optical geometry, separates sample gas from electronics cooling and allows the wells to be replaced. Optical simulations supported a single LEE 101 layer, which retained 70.43% of proxy-green current while reducing LED-derived current to 2.987% of the unfiltered value; airflow modeling guided the inlet shelf and delivery conditions. The reader was assembled, and its acquisition software supports frequency-resolved records and local data export. Assembly feedback informed the revised developer manual. Together, these results establish the prototype and its operating workflow; fluorescence detection by the complete instrument remains to be verified.

36752e204542.text: Monitoring volatile changes around stored produce requires a practical link between receptor biology and an interpretable measurement. Our sensing strategy pairs insect odorant receptors with the calcium indicator GCaMP6f so that receptor activation can be read optically.

3e30342807d6.text: The hardware task is to expose several cell samples to the same gas input and record their optical responses in a compact reader with replaceable wells.

f4f75176fe14.text: A difference between channels should reflect the samples being compared, rather than differences in gas delivery or light collection. We therefore need to control the gas path, keep each well in a fixed position and limit excitation light reaching the detector. Using one photodiode simplifies the detector layout, but requires distinct LED modulation frequencies and digital lock-in processing to recover the excitation channels. These requirements connect the enclosure, optics, electronics and acquisition software.

558a1c8dd774.text: The well simulation predicts unequal collection and mixing between wells: the intended well contributes 88.6–90.9% of the modeled green signal in each LED channel. A brighter channel can therefore reflect collection geometry as well as sample fluorescence. We keep the well–LED–detector registration fixed and specify calibration with the same fluorescence standard placed in one well at a time. These four measurements define a measured 4 × 4 transfer matrix for correcting unequal sensitivity and estimating neighboring-well contributions. Its correction must then recover independent mixed-well standards; the simulated matrix is a design guide, not a calibration applied to the device.

87883648cfaf.text: The project now has an assembled eight-part reader, a tested acquisition and export workflow, and manuals revised from an assembly trial. Its main contribution is the integration of replaceable living-cell wells, a shared gas chamber and frequency-tagged optical readout in one serviceable enclosure. Fixed optical registration makes repeated calibration possible; separate cooling and sample-gas paths keep fan operation from directly setting sample delivery. The removable wells also let us change the cell-contact material without rebuilding the electronics.

f11ed068f204.text: Optical and airflow models turned these design choices into testable targets: the single LEE 101 layer limits excitation leakage, the inlet shelf changes the incoming jet, and the transfer matrix identifies unequal well collection. The next milestone is measured performance: verify ADC response with known electrical inputs, establish fluorescence-standard response and background stability, then test the measured single-well calibration against independent mixed-well samples. Gas-tracer measurements at the wells should separately test the modeled arrival times.

c1156981c42a.text: At matched conditions (3 mL/min, 100 µL/well and D = 10 mm²/s), the open chamber, 12-hole plate and current shelf had normalized downward-momentum proxies of 1.00, 0.57 and 0.69. Their slowest-well t90 values were 51.67, 48.36 and 49.42 s, with interwell spreads of 4.64, 2.83 and 1.62 s, respectively. We retained the shelf: it reduced the momentum proxy by 31% and brought all four wells to t90 within approximately 50 s, meeting our provisional 60 s gas-transport target. Reusing the completed integrated enclosure also avoided another fabrication cycle. The plate reduced momentum more and remains a candidate for the next version.
